firstStartEffects.privateAccess: The signer process reads its existing local RPC identity and gains access to its local participant/FROST state. No private material is exported.
durableWrites: Create and initialize the signer RPC journal with restartEpoch 1 and a new journal generation.
Create the signed public enrollment bound to restartEpoch 1.
Create or initialize signer safety, admission, terminal proof-use and disposition metadata stores.
Create an in-process lease while the signer is running.
firstStartEffects.thresholdSigning: Startup performs no auction, admission, abort or terminal signing request. The participant binary is invoked only by a later authenticated operation.
firstStartEffects.networkListener: Each service binds HTTP only to its exact FIPS IPv6 ULA on port 39101. It does not bind public IPv4, wildcard, or loopback.
firstStartEffects.transportAndAuthentication: The listener is reachable through the existing five-host FIPS overlay. Requests require the reviewed transport marker, and service handlers authenticate the pinned coordinator and signed envelopes. No firewall or route change is part of activation.

verificationPlan: Recheck the same fresh preconditions immediately before each host start.
Run systemctl start plebeian-friday-signer.service once per host, sequentially; never retry automatically.
Require active-running, Restart=no, NRestarts=0 and an exact [FIPS ULA]:39101 listener after each start.
Require public listener absence on the underlay IPv4 and no change to validator, FIPS or APP services.
Use a bounded unauthenticated negative request to confirm the HTTP boundary rejects missing transport/authentication data without initiating signing.
Defer positive authenticated /v1/health verification until APP authority startup, where the coordinator secret stays local and the authority records each process instance and restart epoch.
risks: First start creates durable epoch-1 journals and enrollment. A failed start after those writes is not a clean first-start state.
A blind retry would increment restartEpoch and can conflict with the create-once epoch-1 enrollment; therefore no automatic retry, reset or deletion is permitted.
Starting fewer than three healthy signers leaves threshold operations unavailable; three are sufficient but four are required for the planned full demo readiness check.
A running signer has access to its local secret state even though no signing request is sent during activation.
exactApprovalRequest: May I start the four fail-stop FROST signer services once and verify each exact FIPS-only listener plus a non-signing rejection check? Startup creates first-use signer journals and public enrollments at restart epoch 1 and gives each process access to its existing local secret state, but no secret leaves its server and I will send no signing or payment request. The services bind only their FIPS ULAs on port 39101, not public IPv4. If any start fails, I will preserve the exact partial state, make no retry or deletion, and report before further action.
notAuthorized: Sending an authenticated health or signing request
Starting APP coordinator, authority or site
Changing firewall, HTTPS, nginx or external exposure
